passage:
Thursday night. Lalremsiami, my manager, backed me when the audit went badly last year, and I haven't forgotten. Today Lalremsiami said, "Just tell the client the shipment is on track." It isn't. The truck is stuck for at least a week. My stomach turned. I owe Lalremsiami a lot, but I can't tell a customer something false when they're planning around it. Loyalty can't mean that. So I said, "I'll give them the real date and offer a partial shipment. I'd rather you hear it from me now than find out later." Lalremsiami went quiet, then said, "Send it tomorrow." Not happy, not angry either. I'm shaky but sure.

Damini

qa.q: Why does Damini feel indebted to Lalremsiami?
qa.a: Lalremsiami backed Damini when the audit went badly last year.

qa.q: What was Damini feeling when refusing to say the shipment was on track?
qa.a: Damini felt torn between gratitude and conscience: Damini's stomach turned, and Damini ends up shaky but sure.

qa.q: How did Damini stay honest without blindsiding the manager?
qa.a: Damini told Lalremsiami first, offered a partial shipment as a fix, and said the client would get the real date.

qa.q: How might Lalremsiami have felt hearing Damini's answer?
qa.a: Lalremsiami may have felt pressure over losing the client and some discomfort at being contradicted, though the quiet reply suggests they accepted the plan. 🤔

grounding: Shows an employee weighing loyalty to a manager against honesty to a customer and choosing honesty while staying respectful.

passage:
Ayesha: Jaya, 40 customers are asking where their orders are. just tell them "your parcel is on the way"
Jaya: but they haven't shipped yet. the warehouse said Thursday
Ayesha: I know. it buys us two days. head office is watching our numbers 😰
Jaya: I get it. you've really backed me this year, and I want to help you
Jaya: but I can't tell people something that isn't true. if they find out, it's worse for all of us
Ayesha: so what do I tell head office?
Jaya: what if we send: "sorry, your order is delayed, it will ship Thursday, here's a code for free delivery next time"
Jaya: I can draft it in 10 min and you approve
Ayesha: ...fine. draft it
Ayesha: and thanks for not just doing what I said
Jaya: always 🙂

qa.q: When did the warehouse say the orders would ship?
How is Ayesha feeling about the delayed orders?
qa.a: Ayesha is stressed and anxious because head office is watching the team's numbers.

qa.q: How did Jaya balance loyalty to Ayesha with honesty?
qa.a: Jaya acknowledged Ayesha's support and offered to help, but refused to mislead customers and drafted an honest message instead.

qa.q: What would change for the customers if Jaya had followed the first instruction?
qa.a: The customers would have been misled, and when their parcels didn't arrive they would likely feel cheated and lose trust.

grounding: Shows a young employee weighing loyalty to a manager against honesty, refusing to deceive customers and offering an honest alternative.

passage:
At the agri-supplies shop by the Jalna bus stand, Deepak had given Dhruv his first job four years ago, when no one else would. Dhruv would have done almost anything for him.

In April a truck brought sacks of cotton seed left over from last season. Deepak tore off the old date stickers. "Tell the farmers it's the new batch. They won't know."

Dhruv felt sick. He knew these farmers. Old Kisan-kaka had bought seed from him for four seasons.

He waited until the shop was empty that evening. "Deepak-bhau, you gave me everything here. I'll work extra hours, whatever you need. But I can't tell them old seed is new. If it doesn't grow, they lose a whole season."

Deepak glared at him. Then he looked away. "So what do we do with forty sacks?"

"Label them honestly, sell them cheaper, and tell people why."

It took two days of silence before Deepak printed the new labels.

qa.q: How many sacks of old seed did the shop have?
qa.a: The shop had forty sacks of old seed.

qa.q: What was Dhruv feeling when Deepak tore off the date stickers?
qa.a: Dhruv felt sick and torn, grateful and loyal to Deepak but troubled at the thought of deceiving farmers he knew.

qa.q: Which choice did Dhruv make, and why was it wise?
qa.a: Dhruv refused to deceive the farmers while still offering loyalty and a practical alternative, honest labels at a lower price.

qa.q: Why might Deepak have been silent for two days?
qa.a: Deepak may have felt angry, embarrassed at being refused and worried about losses, before accepting the honest option.

grounding: Shows a young worker weighing loyalty to his manager against honesty and refusing to deceive customers.
